clue.text: Oriental creature with harp represented on a monument?

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for something written on a monument, an inscription

parts.note: E for East, the Orient being the East
a pig is a creature, any animal

indicators.note: represented in a new form, so the letters of harp are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carving of some eastern beast holding a harp decorates a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition describes the inscription by where it sits rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is an inscription carved on a building, statue or memorial stone.

clue.text: Worn out making notes before a charity function

indicators.note: before puts the notes ahead of the function

parts.note: E and F are notes of the musical scale
a fete is an outdoor fundraising event

explanation.surface: Exhausted from making notes ahead of a fundraising event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are musical notes, E and F, not jottings. A FETE is a summer fundraising fair in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means exhausted, enfeebled, having lost vigour.

clue.text: Wanting peace to re-write "Eric" in

indicators.note: rewriting the name with in puts those letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A peace-seeker wants to redraft a piece called Eric.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic means conciliatory, aiming at harmony rather than conflict.

clue.text: One jockeyed for a place on the course

definitions.text: One jockeyed for a place on the course

parts.words: One jockeyed for a place on the course
parts.note: jockeyed for a place sounds like jostling for position, but read literally it is something ridden by a jockey hoping to finish placed in a race

explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred for racing is ridden by a jockey and aims to be placed at a racetrack.

clue.text: Without time to get a rise, quietly remarried as planned

parts.note: P for piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for remarried surrounds the other piece

parts.note: rematch, mated again, means remarried

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: With no time to climb the ladder, a quiet second wedding was all deliberately arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking, and 'to get a rise' makes the reversed time-word rise up the down entry. Tide meaning time survives in Yuletide and eventide.
explanation.definitionFit: Premeditated means thought out beforehand, done deliberately.

clue.text: Inhibition 'making us end a phone call abruptly?

definitions.text: making us end a phone call abruptly?
definitions.meaning: putting the receiver down to cut off a call

explanation.surface: Someone's shyness makes them cut off phone calls without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological hang-up is a neurosis or block, and to hang up is to replace the receiver and finish a telephone conversation.

clue.text: Stories about soldiers in a scene of conflict

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stories go around the soldiers

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Tales of troops in a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA (a collection of anecdotes) and RE (Royal Engineers, a British Army corps) are crossword standbys.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of contest, originally the sanded floor of a Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: Galactic material mostly beginning to expand and freeze over

indicators.note: material as in raw material to be reshaped, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the final letter of Galactic
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Matter from space, mostly starting to spread, ices over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last C of GALACTIC; 'material' rearranges GALACTI into GLACIAT, and 'beginning to' takes E from expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaciate is to cover with ice or turn to ice.

clue.text: Training social worker in dull academicism

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training

indicators.note: in places the insect inside the word for dull

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: Coaching a care worker in tedious scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is an ant, a social insect, not a welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive fussiness over formal rules and book learning.

clue.text: Jacobean dramatist and arrow-maker

definitions.meaning: John ..., playwright who collaborated with Beaumont and Shakespeare
a craftsman who makes arrows, from French fleche

explanation.surface: A playwright of King James's reign also crafted arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher wrote plays in the reign of James I; the trade name for a maker of arrows comes from the French word for arrow.

clue.text: Messenger believed in god? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
says the stated container order is reversed, so the god goes inside the word for believed

parts.note: held, as in held an opinion, means believed
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A messenger had faith in a deity, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'believed in god' puts the believing word inside the god; 'Quite the opposite' swaps the container and the contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official who carried messages and proclamations.

clue.text: Mean to beat up a man with evidence of debts

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to rap is to strike or beat
Simon is a man's name
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Intending to thrash someone who has signed IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat up' looks like assault; 'up' reverses RAP to PAR. IOU means 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimonious means stingy, unwilling to spend.

clue.text: Member's part in getting East Ender intoxicated

indicators.note: the ender of a word is its final letter, here of East

parts.note: high means drunk or drugged

explanation.surface: A Londoner from the East End gets drunk and hurts a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Ender' looks like a Cockney, but it is just the last letter of East, T, joined to HIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper section of the leg, a limb or member of the body.

clue.text: Rejected call to convert into a radioactive gas

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for call is read backwards

parts.note: to call is to name

indicators.note: converting changes the form of the letters into a, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a summons to become a radioactive gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns NAME into EMAN; 'to convert' rearranges INTO A into ATION. Emanation is the old name for radon, the gas given off by radium.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanation was the early chemical name for radon and its isotopes, gases given off by radioactive elements.

clue.text: Loco enthusiast teaches snooker player

parts.note: trains means teaches or coaches
a potter is a player who pots balls in snooker

explanation.surface: A railway fan gives lessons to a man at the snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loco' is short for locomotive, not crazy. Snooker is a cue game, like pool, where balls are potted.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a hobbyist who records the numbers of railway engines seen.

clue.text: Port authority in Ostend originally? That's no help, confound it!

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of Ostend
confounding throws things into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A harbour official in a Belgian port is fed up with useless assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is the fortified wine, not a harbour, so the port authority is a wine buff rather than a harbourmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a connoisseur of wines, so an expert on fortified wine counts.

clue.text: American money order unacceptable at the pay-desk

parts.note: check is the American spelling of cheque
out means not acceptable, as in out of the question

explanation.surface: A shop till refuses a US cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkout is the counter where shoppers pay.

clue.text: Seaman's sweater is found in the Channel

definitions.meaning: a thick knitted woollen jumper worn by sailors
one of the Channel Islands, off Normandy

explanation.surface: A sailor's jumper turns up in the waters between England and France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel is the English Channel; its islands include Jersey and Guernsey, both giving names to knitwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A guernsey is a fisherman's oiled-wool pullover, named after the Channel Island where it originated.

clue.text: How to secure employment providing ammunition for the party

indicators.note: securing something holds it within, so the word for employment goes inside how

parts.note: taken as written
use means employment, as in putting to use
arming means supplying with weapons and ammunition

explanation.surface: A guide on getting a job that supplies munitions to a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is a celebration, not a political group, and 'providing ammunition' is a verb phrase, not a supply depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewarming is a celebration held when people move into a new home.

clue.text: Exceptional ability of one going to America with information

parts.note: gen is slang for information
I is the Roman numeral one
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone talented goes to the States carrying intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius means extraordinary intellectual or creative power.

clue.text: Standard lines written about a dead queen

indicators.note: about means around, so the lines go round the queen

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran railway lines
Queen Anne, long dead, as in Queen Anne's dead for stale news

explanation.surface: Ordinary verses composed about a deceased monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' are railway lines: BR, British Rail, the former national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried on a pole, as a banner is.

clue.text: Part of the Atlantic Ocean — can a ship's timber exist in it?

indicators.note: it refers back to the word can, so the other pieces go inside that word

parts.note: a rib is one of the curved timbers forming a ship's frame
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Asking whether a piece of shipwreck could survive in an ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'can' in the clue, so the ship's timber and its companions go inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean Sea is an arm of the Atlantic bounded by the West Indies and Central America.

clue.text: One container when placed in another

indicators.note: placed in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a bin is another container
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: One vessel is set within a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' refers back to container, giving BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl for holding liquid.

clue.text: Sculpture giving rise to letters in Athens

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A statue causes some writing to appear in the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two Greek letters side by side; 'giving rise to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Some jobs essentially preoccupy…

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain tasks fundamentally take up one's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to fill someone's mind continually, to preoccupy them.

clue.text: … a party lackey given authority.

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
a minion is a servile follower

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a political party's hanger-on is handed power.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue for the surface only; 'party' is a social do here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or control, the power to rule.

clue.text: Aiming to include river in drawing

indicators.note: including means holding within, so R goes inside the word for drawing

parts.note: tying means drawing, finishing level in a game

explanation.surface: An artist sets out to put a river into a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' is a level game result, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying to do something means attempting it, striving toward it as a goal.

clue.text: He appraises animals thus presented to a king

parts.note: asses are donkeys, animals
so means thus, in this way
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A valuer is handed some donkeys as a gift for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for rex, king, as in royal ciphers.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is an official who values property or evaluates claims.
